blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob, the one they called Israel, had twelve sons. Joseph was seventeen, born to him when he was old, and Jacob loved him more than all the rest. And everybody in that house knew it.

verses.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.

verses.text: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A coat can be a blessing and a burden at the same time. Every time those brothers saw it, they saw what they had not been given. Then Joseph started dreaming, and he told them about it.

verses.text: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

segments.speaker: joseph
segments.text: For, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: They hated him even more. Then he dreamed that the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to him. Even his daddy fussed at him for that one. But Jacob kept it in his heart.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One day the brothers were way off with the flocks, and Jacob sent Joseph to see about them. He found them at Dothan. They saw him coming from a long way off, in that coat.

verses.text: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they said one to another,

verses.text: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

segments.speaker: brothers
segments.text: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Reuben, the oldest, spoke up. He told them not to kill him, but to put him in a pit out there in the wilderness. Reuben meant to come back later and take him home to their father.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him;

verses.text: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then they sat down to eat. Can you imagine? Their own brother down in a dry pit, and they sat down to supper. While they were eating, they saw a company of Ishmeelites coming from Gilead, camels loaded with spices, headed down to Egypt.

verses.text: And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Judah said unto his brethren,

segments.speaker: judah
segments.text: What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?

verses.text: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.

segments.speaker: judah
segments.text: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.

verses.text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, it is not over. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "It is not over"] It is not over. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "It is not over"] Not for Joseph, and not down in that pit.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Twenty pieces of silver. That is what jealousy said a brother was worth. It is a hard story to sit with, Church. But it does not end in that pit. Joseph went down to Egypt, and a little later the Bible tells us the LORD was with Joseph there. Hold on to that. We are coming back for the rest.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Genesis 37 and 39:2; the brothers' sin is not softened.

cultural.note: 'His daddy fussed' is plain speech, not dialect; Joseph's sale is told as the wrong it was.
